item.title: A uniform double-factorial construction for consecutive-pattern packings
item.description: arXiv:2611.06937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every overlap $m\geq 3$ and every pattern length $K\geq 2m+1$, we construct an explicit permutation $p\in\mathfrak{S}_K$ such that the number of permutations containing $j$ prescribed occurrences of $p$, with successive starts separated by $K-m$, is $(2j-1)!!$ for every $j\geq 1$. Additional occurrences are permitted. We prove that the corresponding occurrence poset is the ordinal sum of a chain on $m+j(K-m-2)$ elements and a comb on $2j$ elements. An insertion bijection counts the linear extensions of the comb. This gives the uniform representatives requested in the double-factorial part of Question 6 in Section 7 of Blitvi\'c, Kammoun and Steingr\'imsson, arXiv:2610.29846v1. A Lean 4 formalization and its recorded verification data accompany the paper.
item.dc:creator: Zolt\'an Nagy

item.title: Limits of Generalized Magnitudes of Dissimilarity Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.06960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite symmetric nonnegative dissimilarity matrix $D=(d_{ij})$ with zero diagonal, we study the high-resolution limit ($t\to \infty$) of $\mathbf{1}^T(e^{-td_{ij}})^+\mathbf{1}$. We prove that this limit always exists in the extended real line and is rational whenever finite, without weightability or invertibility assumptions. At fixed cardinality, a finite rational polyhedral fan governs rank and leading asymptotics. Consequently, only finitely many finite limits occur, and every limit admits an integer-data realization at the same cardinality. In contrast, allowing cardinality to vary, every rational pair of zero-pattern magnitude and high-resolution limit is realized using dissimilarities in $\{0,1,2\}$; adding the level $3$ permits either infinite limit with any rational zero-pattern magnitude. We also classify all limits on at most four points. Moreover, we derive an exact Schur decomposition valid under persistent singularity. Finally, it is shown that positive semidefiniteness at some positive scale is equivalent to equality of dissimilarity rows for every zero-distance pair, in which case the limit counts the zero-distance classes.
item.dc:creator: Hayato Saigo

item.title: Hypergraphs with zero uniform Tur\'an density at intermediate levels
item.description: arXiv:2611.06964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is uniformly dense with respect to $j$-graphs if, up to a small error, at least a prescribed proportion of the $r$-cliques of every $j$-uniform hypergraph on the same vertex set are edges of $H$. For a forbidden hypergraph $F$, its uniform Tur\'an density at level $j$ is the supremum of these density bounds over arbitrarily large $F$-free hypergraphs with the error tending to zero. For every $r\ge4$ and $1\le j\le r-3$, this paper proves that this Tur\'an density is zero precisely when $F$ admits a vertex ordering in which every $(j+1)$-set shared by two edges occupies the same positions in both edges. This generalizes the zero-density characterizations of Erd\H{o}s at $j=0$ and of Reiher, R\"odl, and Schacht at $j=r-2$, and establishes the latter authors' proposed extension to the remaining nontrivial levels. Consequently, at level $j$, every positive uniform Tur\'an density of a possibly infinite forbidden family is at least $N^{-N}$, where $N=\binom r{j+1}$. The proof combines hypergraph regularity with adjacent exchanges in spreadable random hypergraphs.
item.dc:creator: Heng Li, Xizhi Liu

item.title: Every $r$-regular Hamiltonian graph with $r\geq 17$ contains a second Hamilton cycle
item.description: arXiv:2611.06985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A conjecture of Sheehan states that every Hamiltonian $4$-regular graph contains a second Hamilton cycle. A natural problem is to find the smallest positive integer $k$ such that every Hamiltonian $r$-regular graph contains a second Hamilton cycle when $r\geq k$. Thomassen proved that $k\leq 300$. Improving Thomassen's result, Haxell, Seamone, and Verstra{\"e}te proved that $k\leq 23$. We improve this bound by proving that every $r$-regular Hamiltonian graph contains a second Hamilton cycle whenever $r\geq 17$. Our new idea is to establish a transversal theorem for set systems on a cycle using Harris's results on the Moser--Tardos algorithm for Local Lemma. We then apply Thomassen's theorem on independent dominating sets to obtain a second Hamilton cycle. For $r\ge 18$, we also give some algorithms to find such a transversal.
item.dc:creator: Haiyang Liu, Xu Liu, Bo Ning

item.title: Seeking the dense half in $K_4$-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.07082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices has a balanced bipartition such that neither part contains more than $0.0671n^2 + o(n^2)$ edges. This improves the previous best bound of $0.074n^2$ by Xu and Zhang. We also formulate a conjecture that the tight bound for this problem is $\frac{425}{6498}n^2 \approx 0.0654n^2$, and present a construction showing that it would be best possible.
item.dc:creator: Ignacy Buczek, Andrzej Grzesik, Piotr Kuc

item.title: An improved lower bound for maximal partial Room squares
item.description: arXiv:2611.07117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a new asymptotic lower bound for the volume of a maximal partial Room square of even order $n$. We prove that its volume is at least $\frac{2\sqrt{66}-6}{57}n^2-O(n)$, improving the leading coefficient $1/8$ in the lower bound obtained by Meszka and Rosa. The proof combines two counting arguments, one based on a transversal of empty cells and the other on the graph of occurring symbol pairs.
item.dc:creator: Peter Horak, Dongryul Kim

item.title: Perfect Partitions of Regular Bipartite Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.07118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $I_{n,n}$ be a fixed perfect matching of the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$, and let $L_{n,1}=K_{n,n}-I_{n,n}$. A perfect set of $L_{n,1}$ is a $1$-factorization of $L_{n,1}$, that is, a set of $n-1$ pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings whose union is $E(L_{n,1})$; a perfect partition of $L_{n,1}$ is a partition of the set of all perfect matchings of $L_{n,1}$ into perfect sets. Brualdi, Chiang, and Li (2005) asked whether $L_{n,1}$ admits a perfect partition. Identifying both sides of the bipartition with $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots ,n\}$, the perfect matchings of $L_{n,1}$ are exactly the derangements of $[n]$, the perfect sets correspond bijectively to the reduced Latin squares of order $n$, and the perfect partitions are exactly the perfect matchings of the $(n-1)$-uniform hypergraph whose vertices are the derangements of $[n]$ and whose edges are the perfect sets. We first give, for every $n$, a constructive lower bound on the maximum number of pairwise disjoint perfect sets of $L_{n,1}$. We then show that $L_{5,1}$ has exactly $42$ distinct perfect partitions and that $L_{6,1}$ has at least $82$ distinct perfect partitions; these are the first examples demonstrating that perfect partitions need not be unique. Finally, we exhibit two distinct perfect partitions of $L_{7,1}$, resolving the $n=7$ open problem raised by Brualdi et al.
item.dc:creator: Melanie J. Ferreri, Archana L. Parameswaran, Gexin Yu

item.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
item.description: arXiv:2611.07138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $\Lambda$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $\Lambda$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.
item.dc:creator: Eric Kubischta

item.title: An improved bound for the intersection of two longest cycles in $k$-connected graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.07145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A conjecture attributed to Smith states that in every $k$-connected graph, every pair of longest cycles intersects in at least $k$ vertices. We prove that every two longest cycles in a $k$-connected graph on $n$ vertices intersect in at least $\min\{k,10k-n-30\}$ vertices. Consequently, Smith's conjecture holds whenever $k\ge \frac{n+30}{9}$. This improves the previous bound of $\frac{n+16}{7}$ for $n>33$ and also implies a bound of $\frac{n+22}{9}$ for paths instead of cycles.
item.dc:creator: Juan Guti\'errez

item.title: On Packed Passenger Permutations
item.description: arXiv:2611.07204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An occupied seat in a binary row is called packed if both of its immediate neighbors are occupied. We give a self-contained combinatorial account of this statistic, equivalently the number of overlapping occurrences of 111. An occupied-block decomposition yields a coefficient formula at fixed occupancy and a direct proof of the sharp minimum max{0,3m-2n-2} for m passengers in n seats, including arrangements attaining the bound. The same decomposition gives a rational generating function, recurrences, expectations, and avoidance asymptotics. Full rows, in which every empty seat would become packed upon being filled, are related to independent sets of a path. A neighborhood-union expansion also gives exact counts on rectangular grids. The emphasis is a unified elementary presentation and explicit extremal constructions, rather than a new general enumeration method.
item.dc:creator: Erik Dahlen

item.title: Exact penalties for maximum-edge bicliques in bipartite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.07239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a bipartite graph $G$, we denote by $g(G)$ the largest product $|A||B|$ over pairs of vertex sets $A$ and $B$, one on each side, with no edge between them. These pairs are the bicliques of the bipartite complement of $G$; hence, computing $g(G)$ is the maximum-edge biclique problem, which is NP-hard, as shown by Peeters in 2003. Gillis and Glineur characterized it by a continuous quadratic program, in which a large enough penalty on the edges of $G$ makes the global maximizers correspond to the maximum pairs and the local maximizers to the maximal ones. We propose a new threshold for the penalty, which depends only on $g(G)$. For any penalty at or above it, the global maximizers correspond exactly to the maximum pairs, and every local maximizer with positive value corresponds to a maximal pair. This threshold is never larger than theirs and is sharp up to an additive $1/2$. Spectral and semidefinite bounds give computable penalties; in experiments, a simple local ascent succeeds far more often with the semidefinite one than with the earlier thresholds, although on our graphs that bound already reveals $g(G)$. The penalty formulation, whose optimal value is $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$, is also a copositive formulation of $g(G)$. Strengthening a semidefinite bound of Laurent, Polak and Vargas with the completely positive cone gives exactly $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$, while the doubly nonnegative strengthening is already inexact on six vertices. Finally, P\'olya's linear programming approximations of the copositive cone become finite at an explicit level and converge to $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$ without ever being exact.
item.dc:creator: Youssouf Emine, Bissan Ghaddar

item.title: $s$-quasi-transitive weakly distance-regular digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.07251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A digraph is $s$-quasi-transitive if, for every path $(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ of length $s$, either $(x_0,x_s)\in A\Gamma$ or $(x_s,x_0)\in A\Gamma$ (or both). In this paper, we give a characterization of $s$-quasi-transitive commutative weakly distance-regular digraphs, where $s=4$, or $s\geq 5$ and the cycle polar diameter is at least $s$.
item.dc:creator: Shuang Li, Yuefeng Yang

item.title: Pattern avoidance classes of parking permutations with fixed lucky sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.07267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a parking function, the resulting sequence after all cars have parked is called the associated parking permutation. For each parking function, cars that park in their preferred spot are called lucky cars. In this paper, we enumerate parking permutations that avoid a specified set of permutation patterns in $\mathfrak{S}_3$ and whose lucky cars are the first $k$ cars. Often, the enumeration simplifies to a product of a fraction with a binomial coefficient, recovering existing sequences in the OEIS. For two of the classes, the enumerations are new sequences.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Ferreri, Lucy Martinez

item.title: Rational Tur\'an exponents of a single $k$-uniform hypergraph
item.dc:creator: Chang Liu, Jue Dai

item.title: Gaps in the Most Frequent Sizes of Integer Sumsets
item.description: arXiv:2611.07303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nathanson observed that, for four-element sets $A$ of integers, the most frequent sizes of the iterated sumset $hA$ are separated by triangular numbers. Senger proved this and suggested an analogue for larger sets. We establish this pattern for $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, for every fixed $k\geq3$, where $h\geq2$ is either fixed or grows slower than $q^{1/(2k-1)}$. As $q\to\infty$, almost every such set has the largest possible $h$-fold sumset, and almost every exception has one of $h-1$ explicit smaller sizes. The differences between consecutive sizes among these $h$ values are consecutive $(k-2)$-dimensional simplex numbers.
item.dc:creator: Saad A. Awan, Steven J. Miller, Linh Nguyen, Steven Senger, Elvis Wong

item.title: On the number of edges in quasiplanar graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.07314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A $k$-quasiplanar graph is a graph drawn in the plane with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges. Pach, Shahrokhi, and Szegedy conjectured that every such graph on $n$ vertices has $O_k(n)$ edges. ChatGPT produced a proof of this conjecture. Here, we present a simplified, self-contained version of that proof.
item.dc:creator: J\'anos Pach, G\'abor Tardos, Ji Zeng

item.title: Two-row Schur times Schubert via parallel classes of positroid varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.07351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schubert structure constants are intersection numbers of Schubert varieties. Finding positive combinatorial formulas for these constants remains a major open problem. We resolve this problem when one of the indexing permutations corresponds to a two-row partition. Our approach uses increasing chains, introduced by Sottile for the one-row case, and builds on the skew Schubert functions studied by Bergeron and Sottile. The key step is to connect increasing chains and these functions with the parallel classes of positroid varieties.
item.dc:creator: Tianyi Yu

item.title: The $q$-Poincar\'e sum and separability in a Coxeter group
item.description: arXiv:2611.07365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a finite Coxeter group $W$ and an element $q$ of a commutative ring $\mathbf{k}$, we define the element $\mathbf{L}_{q} :=\sum_{w\in W}q^{\ell\left( w\right) }w$ of its group algebra $\mathbf{k}\left[ W\right] $. We say that an element $w\in W$ is $W$\emph{-length-symmetric} if its coefficient in the commutator $\left[ \mathbf{L}_{a},\mathbf{L}_{b}\right] $ is $0$ for all $\mathbf{k}$ and all $a,b\in\mathbf{k}$. We prove several sufficient criteria for elements to be $W$-length-symmetric. In particular, we show that any separable permutation (i.e., permutation avoiding the patterns $2413$ and $3142$) in the symmetric group $S_{n}$ is $S_{n}$-length-symmetric. More generally, we construct a notion of separable elements of a finite Coxeter group $W$ (which, for finite Weyl groups, agrees with the eponymous notion introduced by Gaetz and Gao), and show that all such elements are $W$-length-symmetric. This is only a sufficient condition; other $W$-length-symmetric elements include (twisted) involutions and elements of dihedral parabolic subgroups.
item.dc:creator: Ben Adenbaum, Darij Grinberg

item.title: The Higman-Sims graph and a geometric construction of the Steiner system $S(3,6,22)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.07407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Higman-Sims graph is the unique strongly regular graph with parameters $(100,22,0,6)$. In this paper, we show that the only distance-regular antipodal double cover of the Higman-Sims graph is its bipartite double cover. Our main tool is a geometric construction of the Steiner system $S(3,6,22)$.
item.dc:creator: Mahdi Ebrahimi

item.title: Prescribed Color Patterns in Tight Hamilton Cycles and Spanning Trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.07421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare transversal and pattern thresholds for two spanning structures. For every fixed $k\ge 3$ and $\alpha>0$, we prove that every sufficiently large $n$-vertex $k$-graph collection with minimum codegree at least $(1/2+\alpha)n$ contains a tight Hamilton cycle with any prescribed color pattern. Hence the transversal and pattern thresholds for tight Hamilton cycles coincide asymptotically. For spanning trees, we show that for every $\alpha>0$ there exists $c=c(\alpha)>0$ such that every $n$-vertex graph collection with minimum degree at least $(1/2+\alpha)n$ contains every $n$-vertex tree with maximum degree at most $n^c$ and any prescribed color pattern. On the other hand, we construct spanning trees of maximum degree $\sqrt n+1$ whose pattern threshold exceeds their transversal threshold by a positive linear term.
item.dc:creator: Lirong Deng

item.title: Connected graphs having maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius
item.description: arXiv:2611.07429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\rho(G)$ denote the signless Laplacian spectral radius of a graph $G$, and let $\mathcal C_{n,m}$ be the family of connected graphs of order $n$ and size $m$. A graph is $Q$-maximal if it maximizes $\rho(G)$ over this family. Motivated by a question of Chang and Tam (2011), we study this extremal problem using scalar identities and coronal methods for threshold graphs. From the Perron equations, we derive the identity $S_G(\lambda)=T_{a,b}(\lambda)$ at $\lambda=\rho(G)$, where $a$ and $b$ are the total numbers of zero-vertices and one-vertices. This yields a one-point comparison principle: for a connected threshold graph $H$ with the same block totals, $S_H(z)>T_{a,b}(z)$ at some $z\ge n$ implies $\rho(H)>z$, allowing spectral comparison without estimating individual Perron coordinates. We prove that every $Q$-maximal threshold graph has character at most three, so its vertex-sequence contains at most three zero--one block pairs. We also show that the quasi-star graph is $Q$-maximal whenever $n\ge5$ and $n-1\le m<(n^2+10n-8)/8$. For certain dense parameter pairs, we construct connected threshold graphs with signless Laplacian spectral radii strictly larger than those of both the quasi-star and the connected quasi-complete graph. Thus the corresponding two-candidate assertion for connected graphs fails in general.
item.dc:creator: Di-Jian Wang, Hong-Yan Ge, Shi-Cai Gong, Bo-Jun Yuan

item.title: Decomposable polytopes with few vertices
item.description: arXiv:2611.07472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A polytope $P$ is decomposable if it can be written as the Minkowski sum of two polytopes that are not homothetic to it. It is well known that decomposable $d$-dimensional polytopes with $2d$ or fewer vertices are the simplicial prisms. More recent work shows that, with two exceptions in low dimensions, decomposable $d$-dimensional polytopes with exactly $2d+1$ vertices are either pentasms or capped prisms. All these examples have a line segment for a summand. In this paper, we extend this conclusion to decomposable $d$-polytopes with exactly $2d+2$ or $2d+3$ vertices. In both cases, all such polytopes, with three exceptions, have a line segment for a summand. The exceptional cases are specified in detail.
item.dc:creator: Jie Wang, David Yost

item.title: Distinguishing invariants of Cayley Graphs, Hamming graphs, and wreath product actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.07497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a nontrivial group that acts on a graph $G=(V,E)$. The total distinguishing number $D''_{\Gamma}(V\cup E)$ (distinguishing index $D'_{\Gamma}(E)$) of the action is the least number of labels required for a total labeling (edge labeling) of $G$ so that the only elements of $\Gamma$ that preserve the labeling belong to the pointwise stabilizer of $V\cup E$ (pointwise stabilizer of $E$). We obtain upper bounds of these invariants for Cayley graphs and under various group actions, including free actions, wreath product actions, and coordinatewise actions on Cartesian powers of graphs. Our first main result shows that, if $\Gamma$ acts faithfully on $G$, with $|V|\geq 2, |E|\geq 1$ and the natural action of the wreath product $W=\Gamma\wr S_k$ on $V^k$ induces an action of $W$ on the Cartesian power $G^{k}=(V^{k},E_k)$, then $ D''_{W}(V^k\cup E_k)\le D''_{\Gamma}(V\cup E)+k-1 $ for any $k\geq 2$. We also establish the sharpness of several of our bounds through examples involving cyclic, symmetric, and alternating groups. Moreover, we determine these distinguishing invariants for the symmetric group action on Hamming graphs.
item.dc:creator: Amitayu Banerjee

item.title: Strict unimodality without log-concavity for partial Petrial polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.07503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a simple graph $G$, the partial Petrial polynomial $P_G^{\times}(z)$ enumerates all diagonal perturbations of its adjacency matrix over $GF(2)$ by rank. We derive a rooted attachment identity and apply it to the tree $R_m$ obtained by joining a new vertex to the middle vertex of each of $m$ disjoint copies of the five-vertex path. We prove that the nonzero coefficient sequence of $P_{R_m}^{\times}(z)$ is strictly unimodal for every $m\ge1$, but is log-concave if and only if $1\le m\le3$. Thus the $21$-vertex tree $R_4$ provides an explicit strictly unimodal, non-log-concave example. For $m\ge5$, the unique mode occurs at degree $\lfloor(149m+85)/32\rfloor$. More generally, for any fixed path rooted at an internal vertex, joining a new vertex to the roots of sufficiently many disjoint copies produces a tree whose partial Petrial polynomial is not log-concave.
item.dc:creator: Ruiqing Feng, Qi Yan

item.title: Structure of adjacency algebras of thin Jordan schemes
item.description: arXiv:2611.07527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that adjacency algebras of Jordan schemes over fields of characteristic zero are semisimple. We then classify the adjacency algebras of thin Jordan schemes over the fields of real numbers or complex numbers. The simple summands of the adjacency algebras over these fields are restricted to specific types of simple Jordan algebras.
item.dc:creator: Yudai Ohisa, Kyohei Yanagisawa

item.title: Generalized Chromatic Polynomials of Cycles and uni-cyclic Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.07568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In \cite{R81}, Read obtained an explicit formula for the generalized chromatic polynomials of cycle graphs using the classical deletion-contraction principle. In this paper, we take a linear-algebraic approach and present a new proof of Read's formula by realizing the generalized chromatic polynomials of cycle graphs as traces of certain linear operators. As an application of this approach, we also derive explicit formulas for the generalized chromatic polynomials of uni-cyclic graphs.
item.dc:creator: Dipnit Biswas, R. Venkatesh

item.title: Probability model of connectedness for graphs with logarithmical degree
item.description: arXiv:2611.07581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$ of order $N$, an integer $k$ with $0\leq k< N$ and a real number $p$ with $0\leq p\leq 1$, let $p(G,k)$ and $t(G,p)$ be the probabilities that $G$ is disconnected when $k$ vertices are removed randomly and when each vertex is removed independently with probability $p$, respectively. We deduce a formula of $p(G,k)$ for Harary graphs and show that the phase transition on $p(G,k)$ and $t(G,p)$ occurs in the class that has logarithmical degree. We also perform simulations on $p(G,k)$ for the Hypercube and randomly generated graphs of the same scale, which suggests that the regularity is a key structural feature that guarantees nice performance on $p(G,k)$. In particular, the Hypercubes have better performance than regular graphs, on average. Surprisingly, Harary graphs, known to be super-connected, have neither better performance than Hypercubes nor even than the average of regular graphs.
item.dc:creator: Huanshen Jia, Jianguo Qian

item.title: Combinatorics of noncommutative harmonic oscillator determinant
item.description: arXiv:2611.07626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain an explicit evaluation of the determinants that appear in the denominators of the integrands for the iterated integrals expressing special values of the spectral zeta function of the noncommutative harmonic oscillator at integers greater than 1. The determinants in question are those of cyclic tridiagonal matrices; their explicit evaluation is carried out, in addition to the inclusion-exclusion principle, conceptionally using combinatorial arguments based on monomer-dimer systems. This explicit evaluation serves as a core component in the study of arithmetic properties such as the modularity of the special values of the spectral zeta function.
item.dc:creator: Masato Wakayama, Wadim Zudilin

item.title: Anti-ribbon shaped Young diagram decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.07715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a sliding procedure on diagrams which splits the standard Young tableaux of a corner-crossed diagram, in particular of a skew shape, along a finite binary tree whose leaves are anti-ribbon diagrams. Combined with standardization, this yields a decomposition of semi-standard Young tableaux into tableaux of anti-ribbon shape, indexed by standard tableaux and governed by their descent sets. As applications, we obtain expansions of Schur functions and Schur multiple zeta functions in terms of their anti-ribbon type analogues; at the level of Schur functions, this is a tableau-level form of Gessel's fundamental quasisymmetric expansion.
item.dc:creator: Hideki Murahara, Maki Nakasuji, Wataru Takeda

item.title: On the classification of $2$-distance-primitive graphs of small valency
item.description: arXiv:2611.07733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A non-complete vertex-transitive graph is called 2-distance-primitive if a vertex stabilizer acts primitively on both the first and second distance neighborhoods of the vertex. Recently, Ruan, Liu and Jin [Discrete Math. 347 (2024), 113978] showed that every connected 2-distance-primitive graph of valency at most 9 either belongs to certain known families or satisfies a collection of further restrictions, with the socle of a vertex stabilizer isomorphic to $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ or $\mathrm{PSL}(2,8)$. In this paper, we resolve these remaining cases and thereby obtain a complete classification of connected 2-distance-primitive graphs of valency at most 9. We also give a short proof of the main result of Ruan, Liu and Jin and identify additional graphs omitted from their list.
item.dc:creator: Xing Zhang, Xue Wang, Jun-Jie Huang

item.title: A Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for dual stable Grothendieck functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.07795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a closed boundary formula for multiplication by power sums in the dual stable Grothendieck basis. The off-diagonal coefficients are signed binomial coefficients supported on corner-connected broken ribbons, which are skew diagrams connected through edges or vertices and containing no square of four boxes. For such a diagram, the smallest power-sum index with a nonzero coefficient is the number of boxes plus the number of edge-connected components minus one. All larger indices give nonzero coefficients when the boundary statistic is positive and zero coefficients when it vanishes. The diagonal coefficient is minus the number of removable corners of the indexing partition. The formula evaluates the stable specialization of Nguyen's Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for K-k-Schur functions. We give two independent proofs, one using Newton's identity and the dual Pieri rules and the other using determinantal formulas and Schur complements.
item.dc:creator: Dang Tuan Hiep, Do Le Hai Thuy

item.title: Three-critical hypergraphs of maximum local edge connectivity two
item.description: arXiv:2611.07856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a hypergraph \(G\), let \(\chi(G)\) denote its chromatic number and \(\lambda(G)\) the maximum, over pairs of distinct vertices, of the minimum size of an edge cut separating the pair. A hypergraph is \(3\)-critical if its chromatic number is three and every proper subhypergraph is two-colorable. In this paper, we give a recursive characterization of the \(3\)-critical hypergraphs with \(\lambda(G)\le2\). We prove that these are precisely the hypergraphs generated from ordinary odd cycles and an explicit family of labeled-tree hypergraphs by admissible Toft splits. This characterization includes a necessary and sufficient condition for a prescribed split to preserve \(\lambda\le2\). The condition involves only cuts in the first factor and the two traces on the split edge. More generally, we establish an exact cut formula for splits at degree-\(k\) vertices of \((k+1)\)-critical hypergraphs, for every \(k\ge2\). We further prove that the smallest member of this critical class outside the family generated by hyperwheels and both forms of the Haj\'os join has eight vertices and is unique up to isomorphism. Together, these results resolve two issues left open by Schweser, Stiebitz, and Toft in \emph{Journal of Combinatorics} (2022): the characterization of hypergraphs with \(\lambda(G)=2\) and \(\chi(G)=3\), and whether hyperwheels and Haj\'os joins suffice to generate all \(3\)-critical hypergraphs in this connectivity range.
item.dc:creator: Jun Yue

item.title: The parity of the number of missing integers in partitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.07908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Missing integers in partitions have been studied by many authors. A missing integer of a partition is a positive integer smaller than its largest part that does not occur as a part. We investigate parity biases for the number of missing integers in partitions and overpartitions. For every integer $c\ge2$, we prove that the coefficients $a_c(n)$ of $(-cq;q)_\infty/(-q;q)_\infty$ are eventually strictly positive and provide an effectively computable threshold. The proof uses the circle method, combining a saddle-point analysis on the major arc with explicit uniform estimates on the minor arcs. Specializing to $c=2$ and $c=3$, and verifying the remaining finite cases, we show that partitions and overpartitions of $n$ with an even number of missing integers outnumber those with an odd number for $n>34$ and $n>27$, respectively. We further prove that, for $n>10$, the difference between the numbers of ordinary partitions with an even and an odd number of missing integers is smaller than the number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts. These results confirm three conjectures of Bhoria, Eyyunni and Santra. We also give a combinatorial interpretation of $a_c(n)$ for every integer $c\ge4$ in terms of colored partitions, generalizing the partition and overpartition interpretations of Bhoria, Eyyunni and Santra for $c=2$ and $c=3$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Julia Q. D. Du, Gurinder Singh

item.title: Clique partitions and distinct color sets in list colorings
item.description:
arXiv:2611.07924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\) and an integer \(m\ge n\), let \(f'(G,m)\) be the minimum number of distinct color sets used by proper colorings from \(m\)-element lists that are disjoint at distinct nonadjacent vertices. A clique-partition assignment gives a common list to the vertices of each part of a clique partition and uses disjoint lists on different parts. In this paper, we construct a graph on \(20\) vertices for which these assignments do not attain \(f'(G,20)\), and a fixed graph on \(25\) vertices for which they fail to attain the minimum for every allowed list size. For every triangle-free graph \(G\) on \(n\ge2\) vertices, we prove \[ f'(G,m)= inom{m}{2}^{
u(G)}m^{n-2
u(G)} \qquad (m\ge n), \] where \(
u(G)\) is the size of a maximum matching, and characterize all minimizing assignments in terms of maximum matchings. For clique blow-ups of each fixed odd cycle of length at least five, we determine the minimum up to constant factors uniformly over the blow-up size and all allowed list sizes, and obtain an exponential separation from the clique-partition value. We also prove that a noncomplete graph \(G\) satisfies \(f'(G,n)=n^2\) if and only if all edges of its complement have a common endpoint. These results disprove the general clique-partition conjecture of Gravier, Maffray, and Mohar (\emph{Discrete Mathematics}, 2003) and its extension by Wu and Zhang (\emph{Applied Mathematics Letters}, 2006), while establishing both triangle-free conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Jun Yue

item.title: Few-Weight Linear Sets and Divisibility of Rank-Metric Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study $\mathbb F_q$-linear sets whose positive point weights belong to a prescribed finite set $A$. The integer $e=\gcd(A)$ always divides the rank of the defining subspace, but the divisibility does not by itself imply linearity over $\mathbb F_{q^e}$. We show that it does in a broad parameter range. Let $L_U$ be an $\mathbb F_q$-linear set of rank $N$ spanning $PG(h-1,q^m)$, $h\ge2$, without being equal to it, and assume that $q\ge m$ and that the minimum weight of its points is $a\ge2$. Combining the theorem of Csajb\'ok, Marino and Pepe on the maximum field of linearity with the lower bound of Adriaensen and Santonastaso for the size of a linear set containing a point of weight one, we prove that $L_U$ is also defined by an $\mathbb F_{q^t}$-subspace, for some divisor $t$ of $m$, whose $\mathbb F_q$-dimension is exactly $N+t-a$. Under a natural gap condition excluding divisors of $m$ in the interval $(e,N-e]$, this forces $a=e$ and the defining subspace to be $\mathbb F_{q^e}$-linear. Through geometric duality, the point weights of the dual of a system are the deficiencies $m-w$ of the rank weights $w$ of the associated code. For rank-metric codes in which the subcode generated by the codewords of nonmaximum rank contains codewords of maximum rank, we show that deleting suitable coordinates yields the $\mathbb F_q$-expansion of a code over $\mathbb F_{q^t}$. We show that the codes in which the codewords of nonmaximum rank generate a subcode without codewords of maximum rank are exactly the direct sums of a simplex code and a code of length smaller than $m$. We derive field-reduction results for two-weight and three-weight rank-metric codes, and show that no gap condition is needed when $m$ divides the length or when the code has only two nonzero weights. Finally, we study two-dimensional codes of length at most $m$ and provide families of three-weight examples.
item.dc:creator: Jan De Beule, Leen Demuys, Ferdinando Zullo, Olga Polverino

item.title: On Grassmann $4$-designs
item.description: arXiv:2611.08047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that there is a unique tight $4$-design in the real Grassmannian $G_{2,4}$, up to the action of $O(4)$. Using symmetric association schemes, we also construct an $N$-point $4$-design in $G_{2,4}$ for every even integer $N\geq10$. For symmetric association schemes of order less than $21$, we classify the pairs of rank-three primitive idempotents defining injective maps into $G_{2,4}$; their images are Grassmannian $4$-designs precisely for four schemes of order $16$.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Samy Baladram, Ryutaro Misawa, Akihiro Munemasa

item.title: Diameter bounds for complexes that are close to flag or close to normal
item.description: arXiv:2611.08071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hirsch problem asks how large the diameter of the dual graph of a simplicial complex can be, in terms of its number of vertices. For normal complexes, the classical bounds are the Larman-Barnette bound, which is linear for fixed dimension, the Kalai-Kleitman bound, which is quasi-polynomial, and the Adiprasito-Benedetti bound n-d, which however holds only for flag complexes. After sharpening the Larman-Barnette and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds, we study how the three bounds deteriorate when flagness or normality is weakened. We give three ways to quantify the distance from flagness, and in each case we bound the diameter in a way that interpolates between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Larman-Barnette bounds. We also quantify the distance from normality by a parameter q, and obtain a bound that is a polynomial of degree q in n. Finally, we conjecture a statement on flag layered families that would imply an interpolation between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Benedetti, Giuliamaria Menara

item.title: The Calkin--Wilf problems on $\ell$-ary partition functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In their 1998 precursor to their celebrated paper ``Recounting the rationals,'' Calkin and Wilf listed nine open problems related to the function $b_{k,\ell}(n)$, the number of partitions of $n$ into powers of $\ell$ with each part appearing at most $k$ times. In this short paper, we answer five of their eight remaining open problems. As a consequence of our results, we extend and generalise results of both Carlitz and Reznick, and answer an open question of Reznick.
item.dc:creator: Michael Coons

item.title: On generalized token graphs with tokens of different colors
item.description: arXiv:2611.08186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize the concept of token graphs, and we call them supertoken graphs. In this work, we consider the variant in which tokens are distinguishable (for instance, by color) and at most one token is allowed on each vertex. We formally define this kind of supertoken graphs and present their basic properties. We study their diameter, in which cases they are Cayley graphs, and their spectra. Moreover, we provide bounds or exact values for the independence, the vertex cover, the clique, and the chromatic numbers of these graphs. Finally, we characterize the cases in which the supertoken graphs of complete graphs are planar.
item.dc:creator: Cristina Dalf\'o, Blas Fern\'andez, Miquel \`Angel Fiol, M\'onica A. Reyes

item.title: The probabilistic bound for perfect hashing is sharp only for binary alphabets
item.description: arXiv:2611.08230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the optimal asymptotic rate $R_q$ of perfect $q$-hash codes, a fundamental extremal problem in combinatorics, information theory, and computer science. Let $B_q=-\log_2(1-q!/q^q)/(q-1)$ denote the classical probabilistic lower bound. We prove that $R_q=B_q$ if and only if $q=2$, establishing an explicit strict improvement for every $q\ge3$ and settling the first assertion of a conjecture of Xing and Yuan (Combinatorica 43 (2023), 347--366). More significantly, we show that, for every $\eta>0$, $R_q\ge B_q+\exp(-(2+\eta)q)$ for all sufficiently large integers $q$. This improves the previously known increments of scale $\exp(-3q+O(\ln q))$ by an exponential factor. We also establish a structural limitation of the concatenation method. For pairwise uniform inner codes of subexponential length, the resulting rate bound exceeds $B_q$ by at most $\exp(-3q+o(q))$. Thus, exponentially long inner codes are necessary to achieve the new improvement scale within this framework. Our proofs combine Fourier analysis, high-dimensional simplex codes, additive permutation counts, and entropy bounds for hypergraph matchings. We further strengthen lower bounds from short inner codes and improve several known numerical estimates.
item.dc:creator: Shitao Li, Minjia Shi

item.title: Open Problems on the Null Space and Image Space of the Adjacency Matrix
item.description: arXiv:2611.08244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Akbari, Cameron, and Khosrovshahi proposed two questions concerning the null space and the image space of graphs. Although these problems have been studied in several cases, they have not yet been fully resolved. In this work, we present constructions of graphs that satisfy both the problems.
item.dc:creator: K Kranthi Priya, K C Sivakumar

item.title: Some polynomial spaces are Euclidean balls
item.description: arXiv:2611.08265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish a matrix criterion for a space to be homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball. As applications, we prove that the normalized space of $K$-Lorentzian polynomials on an arbitrary open convex cone $K$ is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball, giving an affirmative answer to Br\"and\'en and Leake's question, and we also settle Br\"and\'en's conjecture that the normalized space of homogeneous multiaffine real stable polynomials is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball. In addition, our results show that the normalized space of homogeneous $K$-stable polynomials of degree $d$ is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball.
item.dc:creator: Yuxian Dong, Wenle Shi

item.title: Fourier level inequalities on the discrete cube via complex hypercontractivity and Riesz transforms
item.description: arXiv:2611.08289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Eldan's level-$1{:}3$ inequality is a central tool in his second-order correlation inequalities for increasing Boolean functions. His proof is going to Gaussian space and uses an entropy estimate for second Hermite tensors. We give a direct proof on the discrete hypercube. For increasing real-valued functions $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, we prove $$ W_3[f,g]\ge -2W_1[f,g]\log\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}}{W_1[f,g]}\right). $$ The proof combines complex hypercontractivity with the discrete Riesz transforms. We also give a short proof of a level-$1:d$ inequality obtained by Keller and Kindler. As an application, we recover Eldan's correlation inequality with a slight improvement. If $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ are increasing and $g$ is antipodal, then $$ \mathrm{Cov}(f,g)\ge \frac1{24}\,\frac{\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g]}{\sqrt{\log\!\left(4e\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}/(\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g])\right)}}, $$ where the square-root logarithm cannot be improved as shown in the OR--majority example.
item.dc:creator: Fan Chang, Zhenyu Li, Guanghui Wang, Mingrui Wang

item.title: New results on cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.08375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by the work of Poljak, Ba\v{s}i\'c, Damnjanovi\'c, Stevanovi\'c, and Sto\v{s}i\'c used the Kissat SAT solver in a recent paper to systematically determine the small cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers of several families of graphs. By studying the patterns in their data, Ba\v{s}i\'c et al. formulated 15 conjectures on cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers. In this paper, we confirm 9 of their conjectures, trace confirmations of 2 more to existing literature, and, perhaps surprisingly, disprove another one.
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Kucheriya, Jan Petr, Jun Yan

item.title: An improved minimum degree threshold for fractional clique decompositions in partite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.08432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Dirac-type condition for an $r$-partite graph to admit a fractional clique decomposition: every sufficiently large $r$-partite graph with $n$ vertices in each part and partite minimum degree at least $(1 - \frac{1}{30r^2}) n$ admits a fractional $K_r$-decomposition, subject to necessary divisibility conditions. This implies the same upper bound on the asymptotic minimum degree threshold for $r$-partite graphs to admit a $K_r$-decomposition, using a well-known reduction.
item.dc:creator: Sean Longbrake, Michael Simkin, Liana Yepremyan, Michael Zheng

item.title: Tusn\'ady's problem and online two-sample thinning
item.description: arXiv:2611.08455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the sharp order of discrepancy in Tusn\'ady's problem in every fixed dimension $d\ge 2$. The largest combinatorial discrepancy of $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to axis-parallel boxes is $\Theta_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$, extending Wei's planar result and matching Nikolov's upper bound. More strongly, with high probability, this lower bound holds simultaneously for every subset obtained by deleting at most a sufficiently small fixed fraction of a uniform $N$-point sample. We apply this geometric estimate to online thinning of two independent samples of size $n$ from an unknown common distribution, where observations must be kept or discarded upon arrival. For every fixed dimension $k\ge 1$ and expected deletion budget $\rho n$, with $0<\rho<2$, we prove that the minimax expected prefix discrepancy over lower orthants is $\Theta_{k,\rho}((\log n)^{k+1/2})$. In dimension one, the optimal terminal discrepancy is instead $\Theta_\rho((\log\log n)^{3/2})$, giving a sharp separation between the prefix and terminal objectives. For $k\ge 2$, we obtain terminal bounds differing by a factor of $\log n$. The lower bounds are based on Gaussian small-ball estimates for box-incidence matrices, while the upper bounds use stationary Metropolis thinning and, in one dimension, a terminal cancellation procedure.
item.dc:creator: Yuhao Lei

item.title: The Spectral Theory of Cographs: A Survey, Organized by Graph Matrix
item.description: arXiv:2611.06981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cographs, the $P_4$-free graphs, are exactly the graphs obtained from a single vertex by repeated disjoint union and complementation. They contain the threshold graphs, $\mathcal{C}$-graphs and form one of the primary areas for spectral graph theory. This survey is organized by matrix: after a preliminary section, there is one section for each of the adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, eccentricity, Seidel, distance Laplacian and distance signless Laplacian matrices. Within each section we collect what is known for general cographs, for the subclass of $\mathcal{C}$-graphs, and where relevant, for threshold graphs. We highlight the results from the recent years, including the foundational work of Mohammadian et al., Jacobs et al., Ghorbani, Li et al., Niu et al., Lou et al., Wang at al., Mandal et al. Two structural facts are used throughout: every connected cograph has diameter at most $2$, which ties all four distance-type matrices to the adjacency and Laplacian matrices, and the partition of the vertex set into twin classes is equitable for every one of the eight matrices, giving a uniform description of each spectrum (for the Laplacian this is the twin-reduction theory of Barik--Reddy, which we present in detail). Besides surveying the literature, we record several consequences, and mark them as such: an exact decomposition of the eccentricity matrix of a connected cograph, yielding an eigenvalue-free interval for the eccentricity spectrum of all connected cographs; the full distance Laplacian spectrum and its extremal eigenvalues; an eigenvalue-free interval for the distance signless Laplacian valid for every connected graph of diameter at most $2$; an interlacing theorem tying the distance spectrum to the adjacency spectrum. A comparison table across all eight matrices and a list of open problems close the paper.
item.dc:creator: Pallabi Manna, Santanu Mandal, Fernando C. Tura

item.title: Resolving Tusn\'ady's Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.06998v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a lower bound of $\Omega_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ for the worst-case combinatorial discrepancy of $N$-point sets with respect to anchored boxes in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$. Together with Nikolov's upper bound of the same order and Wei's planar lower bound, this settles Tusn\'ady's problem: the discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes is $\Theta_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. The proof combines smoothed product test functions, sampling discretization, and an entropy argument for conditioned Gaussian vectors.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Wengiel

item.title: A second eigenvalue lower bound for the directed configuration model
item.description: arXiv:2611.07104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a high-probability lower bound for the second eigenvalue in modulus of the transition matrix of the simple random walk on a directed configuration model with minimal out-degree at least two and maximal degree not too large. The lower bound matches the upper bound found by Coste (2021) on the same model. Our proof bypasses the need to establish convergence of the empirical eigenvalue distribution. Instead, it reduces the spectral lower bound to a central limit theorem for the trace of the transition matrix at powers much larger than the logarithmic scale, a range that previous results failed to reach. Both the general strategy and the central limit theorem might be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Charles Bordenave, Yizhe Zhu

item.title: Quadratic Extractors
item.description: arXiv:2611.07266v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A quadratic source is a random variable $X\sim\mathbb{F}_2^n$ generated by applying $n$ quadratics to a hidden uniform string. Previously, the best-known explicit extractor for this model required min-entropy roughly $k=n-\sqrt{\log n}$. In this paper, we give an explicit construction for min-entropy $k=\mathrm{polylog}(n)$. Even for the special case of $2$-local sources, where each bit of $X$ depends on two hidden uniform bits, achieving an entropy requirement below $k=\sqrt{n}$ was an important open problem. This is because such sources provably cannot be reduced (in a black-box manner) to our most powerful general-purpose seedless extractor, known as a sumset extractor. Our new extractor bypasses this barrier, providing the first explicit construction to go beyond sumset extraction.
item.dc:creator: Gautam Chandrasekaran, Jesse Goodman, David Zuckerman

item.title: Ultrahomogeneous hypertournaments
item.description: arXiv:2611.07292v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A $k$-hypertournament is a higher-arity generalisation of a tournament, consisting of a set together with an irreflexive $k$-ary relation such that the automorphism group of each substructure of size $k$ is the alternating group $\mathrm{A}_k$. We show that, for each $k \geq 3$, there are continuum-many non-isomorphic countable ultrahomogeneous $k$-hypertournaments, answering a question of Cherlin.
item.dc:creator: Rob Sullivan

item.title: Topological Characterization of Adinkra Heights
item.description: arXiv:2611.07637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adinkras are highly structured bipartite graphs that encapsulate 1D supersymmetry representations. We classify hypercube Adinkra heights with one, two, three or four edge colors using a graph-theoretic notion of equivalence. For the 990 distinct height functions in the case of four edge colors, we show that these classes match modified twisted character classes bijectively and provide a finer classification than spectral Height Yielding Matrix Numbers (HYMNs). We also relate our classification to the physics of the two-dimensional chiral and twisted chiral supermultiplets.
item.dc:creator: Amanda E. Francis, S. James Gates Jr., Digvijay Roy Varier, Ursula A. Whitcher

item.title: A Universal Threshold Theory for Local Properties of Random Linear Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.07661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thresholds for local properties tell us which guarantees to expect from random linear codes (RLCs) and help us carry those guarantees over to structured codes. A monotone property is $b$-local if a collection of at most $b$ codewords can witness its satisfaction or failure, as in list decoding and list recovery. The threshold of $\mathcal P$ is the code dimension at which the probability that an RLC in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ satisfies $\mathcal P$ crosses $1/2$ in a sharp transition. We show that the threshold of a $b$-local property $\mathcal P$ is within $O(b)$ dimensions of the expectation threshold. This is the dimension predicted by the best union bound over covers of $\mathcal P$: families of subspaces such that the span of every witness contains at least one member. This gives a general derandomization statement: Any decreasing local property satisfied by RLCs at a given rate holds at a similar rate for pseudorandom ensembles that fool the cover union bound. In addition to previously studied ensembles, these include codes whose parity-check matrix is sampled from a small-bias distribution. Because our threshold characterization applies to all local properties, this derandomization also reaches properties beyond the scope of earlier reductions, including maximum loads in linear hashing for arbitrary input sets, rank-metric list decoding, and list decoding from insertion-deletion errors and burst errors. Our theorem unifies and strengthens prior works on row-symmetric and coordinate-wise linear characterizations, which located the threshold to within $O(q^{2b}\log_q n)$ and $O(b^2+nb/\log_2 q)$ dimensions, respectively. We obtain $O(b)$ error for every $b$-local property, independently of alphabet size. Under suitable pseudorandomness bounds, the rate loss vanishes for every $b=o(n)$, compared to $b=O(\log n)$ for earlier frameworks.
item.dc:creator: Vinayak M. Kumar, Ray Li, Jonathan Mosheiff, Gilad Shavit

item.title: Web bases for the Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{gl}(1|1)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.07664v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Queffelec--Sartori and Tubbenhauer--Vaz--Wedrich give a diagrammatic web category via generators and relations to describe the subcategory of Rep($\mathfrak{gl}(m|n)$) generated by tensor products of exterior powers of the defining representation. We construct the first explicit bases for homomorphism spaces in the web category for $\mathfrak{gl}(1|1)$, giving an alternative diagrammatic presentation of this web category, and explore connections to the combinatorics of planar networks. Our basis comes equipped with an algorithm to decompose any web into a linear combination of basis webs, giving an effective way to compute in the $\mathfrak{gl}(1|1)$-skein theory.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Enugandla

item.title: Isomorphisms and automorphisms of minimal comaximal hypergraphs of commutative rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.07992v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with exactly $n\ge 2$ maximal ideals and let $k\ge 2$. We study the minimal $k$-uniform comaximal hypergraph $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$, whose vertices are the nonunits outside the Jacobson radical and whose edges are the irredundant $k$-element comaximal families. For $2\le k\le n$ we show that $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$ is a blow-up of the hypergraph of irredundant $k$-coverings of $\{1,\dots,n\}$, and that its reduced form reconstructs the maximal ideals up to permutation; for $k>n$ there are no edges. We obtain a general description of $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{H}_k(R))$ and characterize isomorphisms of such hypergraphs. For $3\le k\le n$ its automorphism group properly contains that of the comaximal graph, and for finite rings with $n\ge 3$ and every $2\le k\le n$, $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$ has the same isomorphism invariants as the comaximal graph, namely $|J(R)|$ and $R/J(R)$. The case $k=2$ recovers and extends the automorphism results for comaximal graphs obtained previously. We also compare the minimal and non-minimal comaximal hypergraphs and identify a condition under which the latter has the same automorphism group and isomorphism invariants as the comaximal graph. The same method determines the vertex set and the automorphism group of the $k$-zero-divisor hypergraph of a product of integral domains, and shows that for finite products of finite fields this hypergraph determines the ring.
item.dc:creator: Elham Mehdi-Nezhad

item.title: Universal $x$-$y$ duality in equivariant topological recursion and quartic Kontsevich model
item.description: arXiv:2611.08018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Topological recursion is a universal procedure that generates an infinite family of multi-differentials with different interpretations in various areas of mathematics. Recently, a new understanding of topological recursion has emerged from $x$-$y$ duality, which relates two such families through explicit formulae. We study $x$-$y$ duality, its parametrised version, and symplectic duality in the setting of equivariant topological recursion. We explicitly analyse the pole structure of the resulting dual families and provide recursive formulae for the different types of polar parts. In contrast to classical topological recursion, the dual family has additional poles at fixed points of the group action, and at anti-diagonals determined by the group action. We show that the partition function $Z_P(E)=\int_{H_N} e^{-N\,\mathrm{Tr}(E\Phi^2+P(\Phi))}d\Phi$ of the Kontsevich matrix model with arbitrary potential $P$, where $d\Phi$ is the Lebesgue measure on Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices and $E$ a positive matrix, admits a Fock space realisation related to the character expansion of the IZHC integral. The Fock space framework provides two mutually $X$-$Y$ dual families of multi-differentials relative to an implicitly defined spectral curve $(X,Y)$. The solution $Y(X)$ succeeds for the quartic Kontsevich model with potential $P(\Phi)=\frac{\lambda}{4}\Phi^4$. We identify a network of duality transformations and symplectic shifts which relate the quartic Kontsevich model with the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant spectral curve. The proposed construction yields a conjectural all-genus solution to the quartic Kontsevich model, which reproduces recursive structures previously established for genus $g\leq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Hock, Jakob Lindner, Raimar Wulkenhaar

item.title: Domination and maximal intersecting families in comaximal graphs of commutative rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.08022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The comaximal graph $\mathcal{G}(R)$ of a commutative ring $R$ has as vertices the nonunits outside the Jacobson radical, two being adjacent if they generate $R$ as an ideal. For rings with $k\ge 4$ maximal ideals, only the bounds $2\le\gamma(\mathcal{G}(R))\le k$ were known, to our knowledge. We prove $\gamma=\gamma_t=\gamma_c=k$ whenever $3\le k<\infty$, without finiteness or Artinian hypotheses, classify the minimum dominating sets, and determine the domatic number. Independent dominating sets correspond to maximal intersecting families of subsets of $\{1,\dots,k\}$; we obtain a closed formula for the independent domination number of every finite non-local ring, which can be exponentially larger than the domination number. The proofs rest on the class sizes of the blow-up description of $\mathcal{G}(R)$ due to Moconja and Petrovi\'c, which we determine for every ring with finitely many maximal ideals, finite or infinite; with them, domination problems on $\mathcal{G}(R)$ become weighted extremal problems on subsets of $\{1,\dots,k\}$, and the formula for the independent domination number follows from the multiplicative form of these sizes. We also treat rings with infinitely many maximal ideals, graph polynomials, and lattices whose maximal ideals are prime.
item.dc:creator: Elham Mehdi-Nezhad

item.title: The universal property of the decomposition space of quasisymmetric functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08063v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile showed that the coalgebra of quasisymmetric functions is terminal among connected graded coalgebras with a zeta function. After developing the notions of gradings and zeta functions for decomposition spaces, we establish an objective homotopic version of this result. Namely, the decomposition space $Q$ of quasisymmetric functions is terminal: for any conservatively graded decomposition space $X$ with zeta function $F$, there is a unique graded ikeo-culf span $X \leftarrow W \rightarrow Q$ inducing $F$ from the special zeta function on $Q$. More generally, for gradings in any complete decomposition space $M$ with indecomposable identities, the terminal object is $J(M)$, the free decomposition space on the nondegenerate simplices of $M$; the quasisymmetric case is $Q=J(B\mathbb{N})$.
item.dc:creator: Philip Hackney, Joachim Kock, Jan Steinebrunner

item.title: Idiosynchromatic Poetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.08079v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove equivalences of asymmetric partition relations involving natural numbers and products of weakly compact cardinals $\kappa$, infinite cardinals $\lambda<\kappa$ and natural numbers to certain classes of finitary problems in the theory of edge-coloured digraphs. We are able to determine three classes of Ramsey numbers exactly, typical examples in these classes are $r(\omega^2 2, 3)$, $r(\kappa\lambda 2, 3)$ and $r(\kappa\lambda 3, 3)$. We moreover provide general upper bounds for $r(\omega^2 m, 3)$ and $r(\kappa\lambda m, n)$.
item.dc:creator: Thilo Weinert

item.title: First-Order Model Checking on Monadically Dependent Graph Classes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08143v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Monadically dependent graph classes are those in which first-order logic cannot encode all graphs. They include all nowhere dense classes and all classes of bounded twin-width. We show that first-order model checking is fixed-parameter tractable on every monadically dependent graph class. Together with the known hardness result for hereditary classes that are not monadically dependent, this gives a complete characterization of the hereditary graph classes with fixed-parameter tractable first-order model checking. This resolves a central open problem in algorithmic model theory. Our proof combines ideas from structural graph theory (graph decompositions), finite model theory (locality of first-order logic), and model theory (counting types). In particular, we show that in monadically dependent classes, tuples of fixed length have only $|U|^{O(1)}$ types of fixed quantifier rank over any set of parameters $U$.
item.dc:creator: Jan Dreier, Nikolas M\"ahlmann, Szymon Toru\'nczyk

item.title: All minimum cuts of symmetric submodular functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute Cunningham's canonical decomposition of a symmetric submodular function on $n$ elements in $O(n^3)$ time. The decomposition represents all minimum cuts in linear space. For the pair $s,t$ produced by Queyranne's algorithm, we construct in $O(n^2)$ time a digraph representing exactly the minimum $st$-cuts of the function. Using this construction in Chekuri and Xu's decomposition algorithm gives the cubic bound.
item.dc:creator: Chao Xu

item.title: A half-line of Schur idempotent norms
item.description: arXiv:2611.08419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using a family of bipartite graphs constructed by hanging identical rooted trees at every vertex of a highly symmetric graph, we show that every sufficiently large real number is the norm of an idempotent Schur multiplier on the bounded operators on $\ell^2$. This answers a question previously raised by the author.
item.dc:creator: Rupert H. Levene

item.title: On rigid regular graphs and a problem of Babai and Pultr
item.description: arXiv:2502.11421v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph is rigid if it only admits the identity endomorphism. We show that for every $d\ge 3$ there exist infinitely many mutually rigid $d$-regular graphs of arbitrary odd girth $g\geq 7$. Moreover, we determine the minimum order of a rigid $d$-regular graph for every $d\ge 3$. This provides strong positive answers to a question of van der Zypen [https://mathoverflow.net/q/296483, https://mathoverflow.net/q/321108]. Further, we use our construction to show that every finite monoid is isomorphic to the endomorphism monoid of a regular graph. This solves a problem of Babai and Pultr [J. Comb. Theory, Ser. B, 1980].
item.dc:creator: Kolja Knauer, Gil Puig i Surroca

item.title: Global patterns in signed permutations
item.description: arXiv:2504.13108v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Global permutation patterns have recently been shown to characterize important properties of a Coxeter group. Here we study global patterns in the context of signed permutations, with both characterizing and enumerative results. Surprisingly, many properties of signed permutations may be characterized by avoidance of the same set of patterns as the corresponding properties in the symmetric group. We also extend previous enumerative work of Egge, and our work has connections to the Garfinkle--Barbasch--Vogan correspondence, the Erd\H{o}s--Szekeres theorem, and well-known integer sequences.
item.dc:creator: Owen John Levens, Joel Brewster Lewis, Bridget Eileen Tenner

item.title: The only Class 0 Flower snark is the smallest
item.description: arXiv:2505.22941v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In graph pebbling, pebbles are distributed across the vertices of a graph. A pebbling move consists of removing two pebbles from one vertex and adding one pebble to an adjacent vertex. The pebbling number is the minimum number $t$ such that, regardless of how the $t$ pebbles are initially placed, it is always possible to perform a sequence of moves that results in at least one pebble placed on any specified target vertex. Graphs whose pebbling number is equal to the number of vertices are called Class~$0$ and provide a challenging set of graphs that resist being characterized. In this note, we answer a question recently proposed by the pioneering study on the pebbling number of snark graphs: we prove that the smallest Flower snark $J_3$ is Class~$0$, establishing that $J_3$ in fact is the only Class~$0$ Flower snark. that systematically reduce the space of pebble configurations. Our bound-based approach shows particular promise for diameter $3$ graphs, where the neighborhood structure remains sufficiently constrained to enable effective analysis.
item.dc:creator: Guilherme Adamatti Bridi, Andr\'e Luis Alves Martins, Franklin de Lima Marquezino, Celina Miraglia Herrera de Figueiredo

item.title: Orthomesy and promotion on self-dual posets
item.description: arXiv:2508.19440v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the notion of orthomesy, which is related to homomesy, a central phenomenon in dynamical algebraic combinatorics. An orbit is said to be orthomesic with respect to a statistic if the orbit's average statistic value is equal to the global average. We particularly focus on the action of promotion on increasing labelings of certain fence posets called zig-zag posets, and two statistics, the antipodal sum statistic and the total sum statistic. We classify all of the orthomesic promotion orbits for the zig-zag poset with four elements. Along the way, we investigate how homomesy of one action can be used to find orthomesic orbits for another action, for the same fixed statistic. We prove several general results which can be used to find infinite families of orthomesic orbits for any self-dual poset that has an order-reversing involution.
item.dc:creator: Esther Banaian, Emily Barnard, Sunita Chepuri, Jessica Striker

item.title: Palettes determine relative Tur\'an densities for ordered graphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.21571v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reiher, R\"odl, Sales, and Schacht initiated the study of relative Tur\'an densities of ordered graphs and showed that it is more subtle and interesting than the unordered case. For an ordered graph $F$, its relative Tur\'an density, $\rho_{<}(F)$, is the greatest $\alpha$ such that every ordered graph $G$ has an $F$-free subgraph with at least $\alpha e(G)$ edges. We show that $\rho_{<}(F)$ is determined by a minimal palette construction for $F$ and give a finite algorithm for computing it exactly. This has many applications: in particular we resolve two problems of Reiher, R\"odl, Sales and Schacht and three problems of King et al. Moreover, in the course of the proof we show that $\rho_{<}(F)$ is equal to another natural parameter, namely the uniform Tur\'an density of $F$, which is the infimum $\alpha$ such that every ordered graph with density at least $\alpha$ between any two large intervals contains a copy of $F$.
item.dc:creator: Domagoj Brada\v{c}, Lior Gishboliner, Freddie Illingworth, Oliver Janzer, Arjun Ranganathan, Leo Versteegen, Ella Williams

item.title: More minor summation formulae
item.description: arXiv:2603.21021v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove determinantal-Pfaffian formulae that simultaneously generalise the Pfaffian minor summation formula of Ishikawa and Wakayama and Byun's recent minor summation formula. These formulae are based on factorisation formulae for the determinant of the sum of a skew-symmetric matrix and a rank-1 matrix. Applications include a Cauchy-type identity for skew Schur functions.
item.dc:creator: Shane Chern, Theresia Eisenk\"olbl, Ilse Fischer, Moritz Gangl, Mona Gatzweiler, \'Alvaro Guti\'errez, Christian Krattenthaler, Nishu Kumari, Markus Reibnegger, Marcus Sch\"onfelder, Atsuro Yoshida

item.title: Domination in Johnson graphs J(n, 3) for odd n
item.description: arXiv:2606.10326v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2025 Cornet, Dravec, and Torres determined the domination number $\gamma(J(n,3))$ of the Johnson graph for every even $n \ge 6$, expressing it as a closed form $\phi_n$ in terms of Fort-Hedlund covering numbers, and conjectured the same value for odd $n$. We prove this conjecture: $\gamma(J(n,3)) = \phi_n$ for every odd $n \ge 7$. A dominating set of $J(n,3)$ is the same as a lotto design $\mathrm{LD}(n,3,3,2)$, and the lotto numbers $L(n,3,3,2)$, and hence $\gamma(J(n,3))$, were already determined for every $n$ by Bate (1978) and by Brouwer (1981); a short degree argument of F\"uredi, Sz\'ekely, and Zubor (1996) gives the same lower bound for all $n \not\equiv 9, 10 \pmod{12}$. The contribution of this paper is therefore a new proof of the odd case, carried out within the bijective framework of Cornet, Dravec, and Torres.
item.dc:creator: Seung-ah Lee, Semin Oh

item.title: HJ numbers revisited
item.description: arXiv:2607.14732v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hales-Jewett theorem is well known. We prove a primitive recursive bound, in fact an $\clE^5$ one, for the density version. In preparation we deal with what was the main induction step in the old proof of Hales-Jewett as a result in its own right with better bounds. Also in improving our bounds.
item.dc:creator: Saharon Shelah

item.title: Adjacency-degree algebras and spectral determination of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2607.21494v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with adjacency matrix $A$ and degree matrix $D$. Applying $A$ and $D$ repeatedly to the all-ones vector produces a space $M_G$ of functions on the vertices, and these functions are constant on the orbits of the automorphism group. We call $G$ AD-observable if $M_G$ contains the indicator vector of every orbit, and AD-separable if the functions in $M_G$ separate the orbits. Forests are AD-observable, by McKay's leaf-pruning argument. Our main result is that for every cograph, $M_G$ is spanned by the indicator vectors of the cells of the stable partition of color refinement. Hence a cograph is AD-observable, or equivalently AD-separable, exactly when color refinement finds its orbits, and we describe these cographs by their cotrees. We also show that two cographs with the same number of vertices and the same homomorphism counts from all caterpillars have the same counts from all trees. The main result does not extend to distance-hereditary graphs: we give two such graphs on nine vertices that are AD-separable but not AD-observable.
item.dc:creator: Zhipeng Lu, Pengxiang Li

item.title: Random Cayley sum hypergraphs and $k$-fold sumsets
item.description: arXiv:2610.08629v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We denote by $f_k(\Gamma)$ the largest integer with the property that every subset of a finite abelian group $\Gamma$ of size at least $|\Gamma| - f_k(\Gamma)$ is a $k$-fold sumset. Extending a recent result of Alon and Pham, we prove that $$ f_k(\Gamma) \leq \widetilde{O} \left(n^{(2k-1)/(4k-3)}\right) $$ holds for all finite abelian groups $\Gamma$ and integers $k \geq 2$, where $n = |\Gamma|$. Additionally, we also show that the lower bound $f_k(\Gamma) \geq \widetilde{\Omega} \left(n^{1/k}\right)$ holds if $\Gamma$ has no nontrivial element of order dividing $k$. Our upper bound improves a previous result of Balogh, Liu, and Sharifzadeh, and recovers the bound of Alon and Pham in the case $k = 2$. The proof relies on a new upper bound for the independence number of random Cayley sum hypergraphs, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Jihyo Chae, Hyunwoo Lee

item.title: Quadratic-size Random Permutations are Universal
item.description: arXiv:2610.13530v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A permutation is $n$-universal if it contains every permutation of length $n$ as a pattern. We prove that a uniformly random permutation of length $32n^2$ is $n$-universal with probability at least $1-\exp(-n/25)$ for all sufficiently large $n$. This removes a $\log\log n$ factor from an earlier result of He and Kwan~\cite{He-Kwan} and resolves an open problem of Alon~\cite{Alon2016}. The proof was found by GPT-6 Pro.
item.dc:creator: Yu Chen, Yiting Wang

item.title: $2$-Large Sets and Nil-Bohr Recurrence: A Disproof of the $2$-Large Is Large Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.16605v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $r$-large if every $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every $2$-large set is a set of nil-Bohr recurrence, i.e., it meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. Furthermore, we show that a piecewise syndetic set is $2$-large if and only if it is nil-Bohr recurrent. From this, we show that a small modification of a set constructed by the first author is $2$-large but not $3$-large, thereby disproving the $2$-large is large conjecture of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also deduce that the family of $2$-large sets is not partition regular, thereby answering another question of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood $B$ of $0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, restricting the common difference to $B$ increases the extremal number for $k$-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of $1+\varepsilon$, provided $k$ is sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss, Sohail Farhangi

item.title: Proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: an exposition
item.description: arXiv:2610.34444v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number of the complete graph $K_n$ is exactly $\frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor$. We present a streamlined variant of the proof of this conjecture recently announced by OpenAI (2026). Although the original proof is relatively short, it is quite difficult to follow. We simplify several steps and provide a concise and accessible exposition of the proof. We also combine this new result with known reductions to determine the crossing numbers of several other graph families.
item.dc:creator: Martin Balko

item.title: Finding solutions with the Borsuk-Ulam theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.39092v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many problems in nonlinear analysis, game theory, economics, and geometry have existence proofs based on Brouwer's fixed point theorem or the Borsuk--Ulam theorem. We study a common numerical approach: deform a problem with one known solution into the desired problem and follow its zeros. A constructive reduction of fixed points to odd spherical zeros makes the approach available to a broad class of problems, including finite-dimensional Galerkin systems, periodic solutions, Nash and economic equilibria, and geometric mass partitions, subject to the regularity and approximation requirements of each formulation. On the sphere, a linear projection supplies an explicit starting model with one antipodal pair of zeros. We give conditions for tracking the resulting curve, allowing turns in the deformation parameter, and relate computational work to accuracy and conditioning along the path. A family of linear models parametrized by antipodal pairs reaches every regular spherical solution from an open set of starts. This simple parameter space provides a basis for exploring multiple solutions; a finite search for all solutions needs additional coverage information. For mass partitions of finite point sets, each continuation step has cost proportional to the number of points in fixed dimension.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R. Musin

item.title: Bounds on the maximum denominator of fractional chromatic numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.41771v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a positive rational number $x=p/q$, where $p$ and $q$ are coprime positive integers, let $\operatorname{den}(x)=q$. For a positive integer $n$, let $\operatorname{sd}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{den}(\chi_f(G)): |V(G)|=n\}$. Let $D(n)=2^{-n}(n+1)^{(n+1)/2}$. It was proved by Alon, Tuza and Voigt that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)$. In this paper, we prove that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)n^{-\frac12\log_2 n+\frac14\log_2\log_2 n+O(1)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For the lower bound on $\operatorname{sd}(n)$, it was recently proved by Bonamy, Hylasov\'a, Kaiser and Sereni that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge\sqrt{2}$. We prove that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge 3^{1/3}>\sqrt{2}$.
item.dc:creator: Xinbo Xu, Xuding Zhu

item.title: The strong fractional choice number can exceed the choice number by an arbitrarily large amount
item.description: arXiv:2611.03236v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Erd\H{o}s, Rubin and Taylor asked whether $(a,b)$-choosability implies $(am,bm)$-choosability for all positive integers $a,b,m$. Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni disproved this for $(a,b,m)=(4,1,2)$ and asked whether a $3$-choosable graph can fail to be $(6,2)$-choosable. Following Jiang and Zhu, Li and Zhu asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(kb+1,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $k,b$. Equivalently, Xu and Zhu asked whether $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)\le\operatorname{ch}(G)$ for every graph $G$. Here $\operatorname{ch}(G)$ is the choice number, and $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)$ is the strong fractional choice number, defined as the infimum of real $r$ such that $G$ is $(a,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $a,b$ with $a/b\ge r$.
