We prove that, for all integers $t\ge0$ and $b\ge7t+2$, there is a planar graph $G$ with $\operatorname{ch}(G)=3$ that is not $(3b+t,b)$-choosable. This answers all these questions and gives a lower bound of $1/7$ on the supremum of $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)-\operatorname{ch}(G)$ over planar graphs of choice number three. For all integers $k\ge4$, $t\ge0$ and $b\ge3t+2$, we construct a graph $G$ with $\operatorname{ch}(G)=k$ that is not $(kb+t,b)$-choosable, using the six-vertex wheel $W_5$ as its core gadget. This gives the corresponding lower bound $1/3$ for each $k\ge4$. The case $t=0$ and $b=2$ recovers the main result of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni. Finally, for every integer $t\ge1$, there are a positive integer $k$ and a $k$-choosable graph that is not $(8k+4t-1,8)$-choosable. Thus the difference between the strong fractional choice number and the choice number is unbounded, even with multiplicity fixed at eight. We further prove $k+\Omega(\log k)\le\sup\{\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G):\operatorname{ch}(G)=k\}\le2^{(1+o(1))k}$ as $k$ tends to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Yangyan Gu, Rongxing Xu

item.title: A family of symmetric counterexamples to the bent sum decomposition conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.06744v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we provide an infinite family of counterexamples to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions. The conjecture states that every Boolean function in an even number of variables $n$ of algebraic degree at most $n/2$ can be written as the sum of two bent functions. We show that for every $n=2^k\geq 8$, the symmetric function $F_n=1+\sigma_2+\sigma_4+\sigma_6+\cdots+\sigma_{n/2}$ has degree $n/2$ and cannot be written as a sum of at most two bent functions. Here $\sigma_j$ is the elementary symmetric Boolean polynomial of degree $j$. Furthermore, we show that the eight-variable member of this family can be represented as the sum of exactly three bent functions. Using the connection between bent-sum decompositions and derivatives of bent functions, we also obtain an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions that cannot be derivatives of bent functions.
item.dc:creator: M\'at\'e R\'obert Kepes, Anita Kercs\'o-Moln\'ar, Andr\'as Viczi\'an

item.title: Functional relations for higher-order free cumulants
item.description: arXiv:2112.12184v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish the functional relations between generating series of higher-order free cumulants and moments in higher-order free probability, solving an open problem posed fifteen years ago by Collins, Mingo, \'Sniady and Speicher. We propose an extension of free probability theory, which governs the all-order topological expansion in unitarily invariant matrix ensembles, with a corresponding notion of free cumulants and give as well their relation to moments via functional relations. Our approach is based on the study of a master transformation involving double monotone Hurwitz numbers via semi-infinite wedge techniques, building on the recent advances of the last-named author with Bychkov, Dunin-Barkowski and Kazarian. We illustrate our formulas by computing the first few decaying terms of the correlation functions of an ensemble of spiked GUE matrices, going beyond the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem.
item.dc:creator: Ga\"etan Borot, S\'everin Charbonnier, Elba Garcia-Failde, Felix Leid, Sergey Shadrin

item.title: On the representation functions of certain numeration systems
item.description: arXiv:2305.00792v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\beta>1$ be fixed. We consider the $(\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D})$-numeration system, where the base sequence $\mathbf{b}=(b_k)_{k\geq 0}$ consists of positive real numbers satisfying $\lim_{k\rightarrow \infty}b_{k+1}/b_k=\beta$, and the digit set $\mathcal{D}\ni 0$ is a finite set of nonnegative real numbers containing at least two elements. Let $r_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(\lambda)$ denote the number of representations of a given $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ in the form $\sum_{k\ge 0}\delta_kb_k$ with digits $\delta_k\in \mathcal{D}$. We establish upper bounds for $r_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(\lambda)$ as well as asymptotic formulas for its arbitrary moments. Furthermore, we prove that the associated Dirichlet series $\zeta_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(s):=\sum_{\lambda>0}r_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(\lambda)\lambda^{-s}$ admits a meromorphic continuation to the entire complex plane when $b_k=\beta^{k}$, and to the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s)>\log_\beta \mathcal{D}-\gamma$ when $b_k=\beta^{k}+O(\beta^{(1-\gamma)k})$ for any fixed $\gamma\in(0,1]$. Within the regions of continuation, we determine all candidate poles, compute their corresponding residues, and locate the trivial zeros of $\zeta_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(s)$. As an application, we resolve several problems posed by Chow and Slattery concerning partitions into distinct terms of certain integer sequences.
item.dc:creator: Nian Hong Zhou

item.title: Flexible $3$-valent graphs of arbitrary girth
item.description: arXiv:2508.16289v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the existence of a finite connected flexible $3$-valent vertex-transitive graph of girth $\ell$ for every integer $\ell \geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Marco Barbieri, Andoni Zozaya

item.title: The Quasisymmetric Grassmannian
item.description: arXiv:2604.24903v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a complex of toric varieties we call the quasisymmetric Grassmannian inside the Grassmannian of $r$-planes in $\mathbb{C}^n$. Each irreducible component is a positroid variety and an $S_n$ translate of a toric Richardson variety of ribbon shape. We describe it as the vanishing locus of equations $\Delta_A\Delta_{A'}=0$ in Pl\"ucker coordinates determined by a new noncrossing combinatorial object we call the quasisymmetric Johnson graph. We give an affine paving, and show that its cohomology ring is a quasisymmetric modification of the Borel presentation of the Grassmannian's cohomology, with fundamental quasisymmetric polynomials playing the role of Schur polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Nantel Bergeron, Lucas Gagnon, Hunter Spink, Vasu Tewari

item.title: Hardness of Counting Orderings: Taking Gadget Amplification to the Limit
item.description: arXiv:2606.29157v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a new elementary technique for proving $\#P$-hardness results under Turing reductions, and showcase its applicability by settling the counting complexity of several fundamental problems about counting orderings in graphs, posets, and geometric configurations. The technique addresses a natural difficulty in counting reductions: when designing gadgets that attempt to enforce a semantic property, the introduction of the gadgets themselves can affect the function to count in complicated ways. In a nutshell, we introduce an amplification parameter $q$ for the gadgets (e.g., replacing a subset of the vertices of a graph by $q$ copies) and show that the limiting behavior when $q$ tends to infinity, or even to negative values, filters out the unwanted effects of the gadgets, which allows us to recover the desired counts. These limits can be computed symbolically via interpolation, after showing that the probability of a random ordering satisfying the problem's constraints is a rational function in $q$. Concretely, with this methodology, we show $\#P$-completeness for counting the following objects: (a) successive vertex orderings, even on bipartite graphs, (b) $st$-numberings of graphs, (c) shellings, even for bipartite graphs, (d) perfect elimination orderings, even for split graphs, (e) linear extensions of N-free posets of height $3$, (f) linear extensions of posets of height $2$, and (g) peeling sequences of point sets. Result (e) settles a conjecture of Felsner and Manneville (2015), and although result (f) was first proved by Dittmer and Pak (2018), we include an alternative proof, using our technique, that does not rely on the result of Brightwell and Winkler (1991) about hardness of counting for general posets. Result (g) answers a question of Eppstein.
item.dc:creator: Marcelo Arenas, Mar\'ia Alejandra Schild, Bernardo Subercaseaux

item.title: The microscopic weighting on a metric space
item.description: arXiv:2607.05349v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the microscopic weighting, a canonical signed measure of mass one that can be associated to almost any finite metric space. The microscopic weighting is obtained as the small-scale limit of the weightings used to define the magnitude function. We give general criteria for its existence, proving in particular that every finite space of strictly negative type admits a microscopic weighting; this includes every finite subset of Euclidean or hyperbolic space and every finite tree. Heuristically speaking, the microscopic weighting distributes its mass as widely as possible across a space, assigning greater weight to sparse or outlying regions and emphasizing points on the boundary. Indeed, we show that on a finite space of negative type the microscopic weighting can be characterized (when it exists) as an optimizing measure for an energy integral determined by the distance function. Alternatively, it can be characterized in terms of the geometry of the Schoenberg embedding. Each of these interpretations also clarifies the information carried by the derivative of the magnitude function at zero. Though our main focus in this paper is on finite metric spaces, we lay the groundwork to extend the theory to compact subsets of Euclidean space. In that setting, we observe that the microscopic weighting must be understood as a distribution rather than as a measure.
item.dc:creator: Emily Roff, Simon Willerton

item.title: Perfect Codes As Exact Minimizers Of Quadratic Discrepancy In q-ary Hamming Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.01134v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Total quadratic ball discrepancy measures the deviation of codeword counts from uniformity over all Hamming balls. We prove that, whenever a Hamming space and cardinality admit a perfect code, the discrepancy minimizers among all subsets of that cardinality are precisely the perfect codes. This extends Barg's binary minimizing result and characterizes equality over arbitrary finite alphabets. At parameter sets that satisfy the sphere-packing condition and Lloyd's integral-root condition for correcting one or two errors, we give an explicit lower bound whose attainment is equivalent to perfect tiling: the discrepancy that a perfect code with these parameters would have. For one error, these include parameters at which the existence of a perfect code is open. For alphabets of size at least four, the discrepancy is an affine function of an energy with a strictly completely monotonic potential; for these alphabets, known universal energy bounds also give these lower bounds, and, when a perfect code exists, known universal optimality results also give the characterization of the minimizers. Over the ternary alphabet, complete monotonicity fails, and we prove the ternary bounds directly at all Hamming parameters and at the Golay parameters, the only nontrivial ternary cases.
item.dc:creator: Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

item.title: Quantitative Tiling Stability From Quadratic Discrepancy In Hamming Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.25716v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quadratic ball discrepancy measures how uniformly a code meets Hamming balls over all centers and radii. Perfect codes minimize this quantity among codes of the same cardinality. We prove a quantitative refinement: at the parameters of every perfect code other than a one-word code or the full space, the discrepancy excess over the minimum is at least an explicit positive multiple of the discrepancy at the packing radius. The latter equals the tiling defect divided by the square of the code cardinality. This defect is the total squared deviation of the covering multiplicity from one. The comparison applies to all codes of that cardinality. For one-error perfect codes, the coefficient is at least one, and no larger constant holds for all such codes; explicit coefficients depending on the parameters can be much larger. The tiling defect also measures the failure of uniform ball noise to smooth a code distribution. Consequently, the same discrepancy excess gives explicit bounds on holes, overlaps, and divergence from the uniform distribution.
item.dc:creator: Valery (Binyamin), Grishin (Yohananov), Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

item.title: Log-concavity and unimodality of cluster monomials in fan coordinates of type A_n
item.description: arXiv:2610.09312v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every cluster monomial of type A_n is log-concave and unimodal with respect to its Laurent expansion in a fan initial cluster. We derive a coefficient formula for laminar interval products arising from compatible diagonals in the polygon model. This gives partial affirmative answers to the log-concavity conjecture of Chen-Huang-Sun and the unimodality conjecture of Chen. Our result for cluster A-varieties also complements Shen's study on the supports of products of canonical basis elements for cluster X-varieties of type A_n.
item.dc:creator: Zhichao Chen

item.title: Mutual-visibility k-colouring is NP-complete for every fixed diameter
item.description: arXiv:2611.01012v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A mutual-visibility set in a graph G is a set S of vertices such that any two vertices of S are connected by a shortest path with no internal vertex in S, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $\chi_\mu(G)$ is the minimum number of mutual-visibility sets needed to partition V(G). Babu, Di Stefano and Lakshmanan showed that it is NP-complete to decide whether $\chi_\mu(G)\le 2$ for graphs of diameter four. We show that the problem remains NP-complete for graphs of diameter d, for every fixed $d\ge2$; diameter two is the smallest diameter for which the problem is non-trivial. More generally, for all fixed $k\ge2$ and $d\ge2$, it is NP-complete to decide whether $\chi_\mu(G)\le k$ for graphs of diameter d. The proof rests on a reformulation of $\chi_\mu(G)\le 2$ for diameter-two graphs as the 2-colourability of an associated hypergraph, and on a reduction from 2-colourability of 3-uniform hypergraphs without short cycles.

item.title: Exact Agreement Expansion up to the Top via Non-polarity
item.description: arXiv:2611.03261v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Agreement expansion asks whether local assignments to faces of a poset that usually agree on a sampled common face must agree with a single global function on most faces. Agreement expansion is exact (approximate) if local assignments need to exactly (approximately) agree with the global function. We suggest a new proof technique for agreement expansion that enables agreement expansion in settings which were previously beyond reach, such as: exact agreement expansion for Grassmannian posets (before only simplicial complexes support exact agreement expansion); agreement expansion based on assignments to top faces of the a complex (before agreement expansion is generally proven only for assignments to low dimensional faces); agreement expansion from one-sided spectral expansion (before, two sided spectral assumption was needed in general settings). Specifically, for down-closed simplicial and Grassmannian complexes, we prove an exact agreement theorem between any two layers assuming one-sided spectral expansion in links of singletons. As an application, we show that full bases of every rank-$k$ matroid admit exact agreement with soundness $O(k^2/[h(k-h)])$ when tested through $h$-element independent sets. We also obtain exact agreement on Grassmannian posets under one-sided spectral expansion, with stronger soundness under a local distance guarantee. Our key proof ideas center around non-polarity of the distributions of local assignments, probed via a random exposure of elements.

item.title: Isosceles sets and two-distance sets in Euclidean space
item.description: arXiv:2611.05421v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isosceles if every three of its points form an isosceles triangle. Erd\H{o}s asked in 1946 for the largest size $\mathrm{iso}(d)$ of an isosceles set in $\mathbb{R}^d$; the answer was known for $d\le8$. Let $g(d)$ and $M(d)$ be the largest sizes of a two-distance set and of a spherical two-distance set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We prove that $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\max\{g(d),M(d)+1,M(d-1)+3\}$ for every $d\ge2$, which reduces the problem to these two classical ones. With the recently determined values of $g(d)$ for $9\le d\le22$ we obtain $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\binom{d+1}{2}+1$ for $9\le d\le21$ and $\mathrm{iso}(22)=276$, and we show that the extremal set is unique: for $d\le21$ it is the set of midpoints of the edges of a regular simplex together with its centroid, and for $d=22$ it is the McLaughlin configuration together with its centre. For $10\le d\le22$ every isosceles set with more than $\binom d2+3$ points is a two-distance set or a spherical two-distance set together with its centre. The proofs start from Blokhuis' decomposition of isosceles sets into mutually orthogonal two-distance sets. Counting leaves one configuration open: a two-distance set with $\binom{d+1}{2}$ points in a hyperplane, the largest number allowed by Blokhuis' bound, together with two points that are mirror images of each other. We exclude it by showing that a two-distance set $T$ attaining Blokhuis' bound in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is unisolvent for quadratic polynomials and that, if $T$ lies on two concentric spheres, then apart from two exceptional cases its two layers are spherical $2$-designs whose sizes are determined by the radii. We also show that the squared distances of such a set are in ratio $(k-1):k$ with $(2k-1)^2\le n+1$ if $n\ge9$. Hence there is none for $9\le n\le23$, so that $g(23)\le299$ and $\mathrm{iso}(23)=\max\{g(23),278\}\le299$.
